statusRationale: No runtime consumer exists for offensive-security tooling in the sandbox: strix scans are hard-blocked by its own gate (DOCKER NOT INSTALLED, measured 2026-10-03, strix 1.6.2 installed and reproducing the banner). Doctrine is knowledge-layer only, like loop-library in r157.
whyNotRevenue: Bug-bounty automation (upstream use case) requires docker-sandboxed execution - blocked here; platform accounts (HackerOne/Bugcrowd), scoped targets and legal authorization are prerequisites with unpredictable, non-daily payouts - fails the measurable-daily-revenue bar.

Strix Cloud route (no docker) requires browser sign-in to an external managed platform and hands source to a third party - the sovereign tree holds the account keychain; not acceptable without operator-level approval.
Selling pentest services requires credentials and a channel we do not have - speculation, not measurement.
activationRoutes: docker-appears: strix -n -t ./ --scan-mode quick --max-budget 10 against a CLEAN CHECKOUT (targets are mounted writable; never scan the sovereign working tree)
ci-route: GitHub Action on PRs with STRIX_LLM + LLM_API_KEY as repo secrets, diff-scoped (--scope-mode diff --diff-base origin/main)
cloud-route: only with explicit fresh operator approval - third-party managed platform

rules.doctrine: Point the review at the risky subtree and state what agents cannot infer reliably: tenancy model, trust boundaries, which inputs are attacker-controlled. Unscoped whole-tree scans are wasteful and shallow.

A reported issue must carry a working proof-of-concept. 'This looks unsafe' is a hypothesis, not a finding; static-only findings are labeled unconfirmed. Same law as the census: no status without evidence.

Exit 0 means nothing exploitable was PROVEN in what was analyzed - not that the code is clean. Check run status, budget cap, and list which paths went unreviewed before declaring health. (Same anti-false-positive family as the init.sh behind-count fix.)
Scan targets are mounted WRITABLE by the tool. Always scan a clean checkout or a copy; never the live sovereign working tree with uncommitted state.
On every change wave, review what changed (diff against the rebase anchor), not the whole repo - whole-tree review on each wave is the expensive habit that kills budgets.

Exploit-validated review does not replace secret scanning or dependency auditing. Keep the dedicated guards running (git.secrets guard pack) and extend to periodic dependency inventory - known-CVE dependencies and committed credentials are structurally invisible to logic-focused review.
Patch the shared cause (the one authorization helper), not the one route, then re-run the check to prove the exploit is dead. Matches census/init.sh fix pattern: measure -> fix -> re-measure.
Never point offensive tooling at third-party services without explicit authorization. Only our own tree, our own services, our own accounts. This is a hard rule, not a preference.
